The Recas didn’t like being called "Recas"—a title reserved for the strongest of the Bonesky clan. He could never defeat the Icho, not even come close.
Once an ordinary, naive Bonesky, he wandered out of his ice cave one day and got lost, eventually encountering the Icho. He sensed the power radiating from the Icho and grew wary, but the Icho beckoned him over. Having lost his rival, the Icho was lonely and asked, "Little one, do you want to grow stronger?"
Driven by his instinct to challenge the powerful, the Bonesky gave a simple, resolute answer. From that day, the Icho trained him like a master, aiming to raise a worthy opponent. Soon, he grew into a Fenrier.
"Master Icho, how strong must I become?"
"Only more powerful than yesterday. Till you become a Recas and defeat me."
He soon became the Bonesky clan’s mightiest and earned the name Recas, yet he still could not best the Icho. One day, the Icho decided to leave, saying he was no longer the strongest. The Recas couldn’t believe anyone but his future self could surpass the Icho.
"That person comes from beyond our world."
"Now I’m off to test myself in the wider world."
The Recas didn’t understand—only that this "person" had defeated the Icho. So he honed his will, aiming to someday overcome both the Icho and that "person."
Then he became a Glynsera, but he never met "that person."
Then you came along. The moment you defeated the Recas, he finally came to understand.
"I’ve met a person of my own."
"I’ve also seen a bigger world."

The Story of the Bloom Festival

When she was young, Baboni would always ask her mentor Avetine why the legendary perfume formula was called "Golden Wish" and why its main ingredient was named "Golden Answer." Avetine would tell her the story of Haidt, the founding perfumer.
————
Haidt was a genius perfumer, and also a strange one.
She always lived in her own world. Perfumery was her way of speaking to the world, and fragrance was the world’s response.
She could hear others, yet never quite understood them.
It was as if her ears caught the words, but her heart could not truly listen.
In search of inspiration, Haidt came to Blitzwood, where she was struck by lightning and fell unconscious.
After waking up, she found herself in a cave beneath a Blitz Tree. She was brought there by a Blazen. A young, clueless Bolty was also there.
Haidt could not understand them.
Then the Blazen motioned for her to touch its bristling tail.
A faint yet layered current of electricity flowed through her.
Haidt withdrew her hand instinctively, but a word echoed in her heart:
Concern.
She could not understand the word, yet for the first time she felt the meaning of concern.
Injured and touched by this feeling, Haidt stayed—living with the Blazen and its cub.
They grew from strangers into family.
Haidt would often go with the Blazen to the Blitz Tree.
The Blazen would send its wishes to the World of Wonders through electric currents, and would also carry Haidt’s voice into the world.
The thunder rolled on as usual, but nothing ever came of it.
The little Bolty was not interested in this routine, as if it did not believe in the World of Wonders at all.
So the days passed on.
Until one day, the Blazen left—perhaps to the World of Wonders.
Haidt went to the Blitz Tree one last time.
She could not generate electricity, but she cried out from the very bottom of her heart.
A peal of thunder sounded, and a branch fell—like a reply from a distant friend.
————
Young Baboni was deeply drawn to Haidt’s amazing story. She too longed to see that World of Wonders.
Each time, Avetine would shake her head gently and call Baboni her "silly little apprentice."
Baboni grew frustrated.
She began to feel that perhaps Avetine didn’t really like her, especially when Avetine mentioned that once Baboni finished her studies, she would leave for a long journey. Baboni felt sad and was convinced that she just couldn’t wait to leave her foolish apprentice.
It was only when she crafted Golden Wish that Baboni understood—what Avetine truly wished was for Baboni to grow into an apprentice she could trust and finally let go, and that Haidt had not named that fallen branch Golden Answer because the branch itself was extraordinary.
Perhaps that thunder was not truly a reply from her friend Blazen.
But the bond they once shared would never fade.
